acceptance: neutralize output for list-nested indented headings renders no <h1>-<h6> on gh api markdown (gfm), with regression tests.
Released in a Theseus version and locked by BenchBox and Theseus.
description:
Found by independent review of Theseus PR #102; present on main 97691757 too. `_HEADING` in src/theseus_reviewer/layout.py allows at most 3 spaces of indent, but inside a list item a `#` indented 4 or more spaces is still a heading. GitHub's renderer turns `x # h - a # h2` into `

h2

`, which breaks neutralize's promise that model text cannot start a heading. Fix in the same spirit as the reference escape: escape a line-start `#` after the container prefix at any indent (a visible backslash in indented code is acceptable), and pin it with render-checked tests. Decision gate: confirm the bypass on current Theseus main with `gh api markdown --method POST -f mode=gfm` before changing code; if GitHub no longer renders it as a heading, drop the item with that evidence. Verification rubric: every probe is rendered through `gh api markdown` (gfm) on the neutralize output, embedded after a list item and inside `report._item`'s assembled body. Cover 4-space, 8-space and tab indents, nested list and quote containers, and setext underlines under an indented line. None may render

-

. Guardrails: change only layout.neutralize's heading escape. The reference, fence and CR handling of #102 stay as they are, briefs without such lines render byte-for-byte as before (golden fixtures unchanged), and the extra escape costs at most a visible backslash in indented code. The PR needs a hosted SHIP and an independent review of the exact head.
